newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Unipetrol swap ratios seen mild plus.
newsitem.headline: Czech Unipetrol swap ratios seen mild plus.

text.p: Czech analysts said Wednesday's announced range at which shares in Chemopetrol a.s. and Kaucuk a.s. will be swapped in for shares in refiner Unipetrol a.s. would be mildly positive for the stocks.
But they said the announcement did not indicate any arbitrage opportunites in the petrochemical companies' shares.

In a joint statement, the boards of Unipetrol, Kaucuk, and Chemopetrol said they agreed to swap one Chemopetrol share for between 1.05 to 1.20 Unipetrol shares, and one Kaucuk share for between 1.10 to 1.25 Unipetrol shares.
An exact ratio must still be approved by general shareholders meetings.

Equity analysts said that because the announced range of the conversion still allowed for overlap in the final decision and did not give a clear advantage to one company, immediate arbitrage possibilities were slim.
But they said that the fact that the boards were nearing a decision on a very complicated issue should give a mild boost to shares in Kaucuk and Chemopetrol.

"I don't see any arbitrage opportunity at this moment," said Patria Finance's Miroslav Nosal. "But now that the exchange ratio is being announced, I believe it will help the shares in both companies."
Tomas Michalek, at Raiffeisen Capital and Investment Prague, agreed that the movement toward a decision would be a plus to the market.
"What is positive is that they agreed on a ratio (range). It's important so that both companies can finally be folded into Unipetrol and more foreign capital can come in," Michalek told Reuters.

Ahead of the news on Wednesday, Kaucuk shares were fixed 11 crowns above Tuesday's close on the Prague Stock Exchange at 1,105, while Chemopetrol finished the PSE's Wednesday continuous trading session 12 crowns higher at 1,106.

According to a 1995 privatisation agreement, Unipetrol shares are still 100 percent held by the Czech government until the merger is complete. Analysts do not expect public trading in Unipetrol shares until well after the deal is finalised.
